facts_found: Common decline reasons include the requested amount exceeding available balance, pending card holds reducing available balance, and the final merchant-presented amount being higher than the initial estimate. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_008]
To resolve a balance-related decline, add funds and retry, and ask the merchant to confirm the amount they are submitting for authorization. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_008]

CODE 51 (Insufficient Funds) is the most common decline; diagnosis requires checking current balance, authorization holds, pending transactions, and the overdraft_pos_enabled setting. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

CODE 05 (Do Not Honor) is a catch-all generic decline requiring investigation in order: card status, account status, fraud alert (fraud_alert_active), then velocity block (velocity_blocked). [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

Velocity blocks are automatic temporary holds triggered by unusual patterns (multiple rapid transactions, geographically distant transactions, sudden spending changes) and auto-expire after 30 minutes. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

CODE 58 indicates the specific merchant terminal has been flagged; the customer/agent cannot resolve it and should try a different register or merchant. [doc_checking_accounts_light_green_account_005]

CODE 61 indicates the transaction exceeds the card's daily purchase or ATM limit; compare daily_purchase_limit and daily_purchase_used from the debit card lookup. [doc_checking_accounts_light_green_account_005]

CODE 55/75 indicate incorrect PIN or PIN tries exceeded; if pin_locked is TRUE, the agent must follow the PIN Lock Investigation Protocol before unlocking. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_010]
CODE 82 indicates a chip/CVV mismatch suggesting physical card damage or possible cloning; ask whether the card was damaged and review recent transactions. [doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_007]
CODE 19/91/92/96 are temporary system/network issues; advise an immediate retry (CODE 19) or waiting 10-15 minutes (CODE 91/96). [doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_009]

Fraud protection may flag unusual purchase patterns, new locations, or large purchases; merchant issues can include a malfunctioning terminal or incorrect card entry. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_023]

Declined transactions are stored with type 'pos_declined' (or 'atm_withdrawal_declined') and can be reviewed in the transaction history to assess location, time, and amount patterns. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_041]

facts_found: get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 is the agent tool used to retrieve a customer's bank accounts (checkings and savings); it requires the customer's user_id. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_009]

get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 returns all account information including account_id, account_type, account_class, status, balance, and date_opened. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_009]

The documented return field is 'balance' (current/posted balance); the KB does not document an available_balance or pending-holds field on the account lookup response. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_009]

The account lookup is the documented source for the account status field used in decline investigation (CODE 05 step 2 'Account Status', CODE 52 'Look up the customer's accounts to check the account status'). [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

For CODE 51 diagnosis, the account's overdraft_pos_enabled field comes 'from the account lookup', and the current checking account balance also comes from looking up the customer's accounts. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

Pending debits are identified by reviewing transaction history for records with status 'pending'; those pending debits reduce available balance but the hold amounts are not returned by the account lookup. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

get_bank_account_transactions_9173 takes account_id (the bank account ID) and returns transactions in reverse chronological order with fields transaction_id, account_id, date, description, amount, type, and status ('posted' or 'pending'). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_018]

get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823 takes account_id (the checking account ID) and returns debit cards for that checking account; savings accounts have no debit cards, so only checking account_ids should be passed. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

Authorization holds reduce available balance but may not appear in the recent transactions list at all, so a hold amount cannot always be read from either the account lookup or transaction history and may require asking the customer or the merchant. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_004]

The standard internal sequence for account-based investigation is: look up the customer's accounts using get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847, then check transaction history using get_bank_account_transactions_9173. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_044]

facts_found: get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847(user_id) is the only documented tool for retrieving a customer's bank accounts (checking/savings); it requires user_id and returns account_id, account_type, account_class, status, balance, date_opened. No lookup-by-account-number or lookup-by-name variant is documented. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_009]

get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823(account_id) is the only documented debit-card retrieval tool; its sole parameter is the checking account_id, and for privacy full card numbers are never returned (only card_number_last_4), so a card number cannot be used as a search key. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

get_bank_account_transactions_9173(account_id) is the documented bank-account transaction history tool; its only parameter is account_id and no merchant, location, date-range, or decline-status filter parameter is documented. Merchant/store text appears only inside the returned 'description' field (e.g., 'ATM WITHDRAWAL - CHASE BANK #2847 CHICAGO IL'). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_018]

The transaction 'type' field returned by get_bank_account_transactions_9173 enumerates posted/pending activity types (direct_deposit, debit_card_purchase, atm_withdrawal, ach_transfer_in/out, wire_transfer_in/out, check_deposit, mobile_deposit, bill_pay, everyonepay, monthly_fee, overdraft_fee, fee_rebate, interest_credit, rebate_credit, fee_refund, atm_balance_inquiry, atm_fee); no declined-transaction type is included in this documented list, and 'status' is only 'posted' or 'pending'. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_018]

get_debit_dispute_status_7483(user_id) is the only user_id-keyed lookup whose records include the checking account_id involved, but it returns only filed disputes and not decline notifications or declined POS transactions. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_035]

get_credit_card_accounts_by_user(user_id) is a documented user_id-keyed lookup but returns credit card accounts only and cannot supply a checking account_id for debit card investigation. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_030]

clear_debit_card_fraud_alert_4892 is documented for clearing debit card fraud alerts or velocity blocks; it requires card_id and reason and does not look up decline notifications or declined POS transactions by user_id. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

The documented internal investigation sequence is get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 followed by get_bank_account_transactions_9173 (which requires account_id), i.e., the transaction step is unreachable without an account_id. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_044]

The generic decline investigation sequence is: 1) card status from the debit card lookup, 2) account status from the account lookup, 3) fraud_alert_active/alert_source from the debit card lookup, 4) velocity_blocked from the debit card lookup — all of which presuppose an account_id/card_id. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

For card-validity declines (CODE 14, CODE 56) the documented step is to ask the customer to verify the card used (including last 4 digits and that it is a Rho-Bank card) and then look up the debit cards for the account to compare — i.e., last-4 is collected from the customer and matched against the account-keyed lookup, not used as a search key. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

Every other documented debit-card agent tool is keyed to card_id or account_id, not to a card number: order_debit_card_5739 (account-keyed ordering), activate_debit_card_8291/8292/8293, close_debit_card_4721(card_id, reason), freeze_debit_card_3892(card_id), unfreeze_debit_card_3893(card_id). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

The documented mechanism for enabling agent tools that are not directly callable is unlock_discoverable_agent_tool followed by call_discoverable_agent_tool with the tool name and a JSON argument string; the KB uses this pattern for credit-card tools (e.g., apply_statement_credit_8472, pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182) and for transfer tools, not for any account/card lookup by number or name. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

The only documented 'last 4' retrieval tool is get_card_last_4_digits(credit_card_account_id), which is credit-card-specific and requires a credit_card_account_id; there is no debit-card equivalent keyed by card number. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_013]

facts_found: Mobile check deposit funds availability depends on the account type and the deposit amount; standard deposits are typically available within 1-2 business days. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_011]
Certain deposits may be subject to extended review, and the customer sees the expected availability date in the app after submitting the deposit. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_011]

After submitting a check deposit, the customer monitors deposit status in the app's transaction history for updates and availability, and should keep the paper check until the deposit shows as posted and available. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_011]

The KB documents no fixed partial-immediate-availability dollar amount for check deposits; partial availability is described only as a temporary hold applying to a portion of a deposit. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_011]

If a deposit has posted but the available balance is lower than expected, a temporary hold may apply to a portion of the deposit until processing completes. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_008]
A temporary hold can apply to part of a deposit, making that portion unavailable until final processing completes. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_007]

An authorization hold is a temporary hold on funds that are not available for use; holds may not appear in recent transactions immediately, but even without a visible line item they reduce the available balance until released or finalized. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_004]

Rho-Bank keeps a temporary hold on certain deposits (e.g., paycheck deposits that are then refunded), which can affect the available balance shortly after a deposit posts. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_004]

Pending card transactions and checks can decrease available funds before they appear as posted, which can cause a lower/negative available balance. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]
To review holds the customer is directed to check both pending and posted activity to understand current holds and recent payments. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

CODE 51 (insufficient funds) requires first looking up the checking account balance, and if the balance APPEARS sufficient, checking authorization holds and pending transactions — merchant holds typically release in 1-3 business days. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

Pending debits reduce available balance, and the account's overdraft_pos_enabled field (from the account lookup) shows whether POS overdraft coverage is opted in (Regulation E opt-in required). [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

Common decline reasons include the requested amount exceeding the AVAILABLE balance at the time of authorization and pending card holds temporarily reducing the available balance; confirmation is via the customer's decline notification and recent activity. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_008]

The available balance is the ceiling for authorizations; a small buffer of up to 5 may be considered for minor adjustments, but spending beyond that results in declines. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_005]

Card purchases and ATM withdrawals are authorized only up to the available balance; a charge above available funds is declined immediately with no overdraft. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_003]

Real-time authorization checks the available balance before each transaction, with a buffer of up to 5 during authorization; beyond that the transaction is declined. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_004]

Green Account (checking) has no overdraft fees and no overdraft coverage — transactions that exceed the available balance are declined — and its daily mobile check deposit limit is $3,000. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_001]

Green Account troubleshooting for declines: verify the available balance covers the full requested amount and review pending authorizations reducing it; if a decline notification was received, check its message details. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_007]

The mobile check deposit tool is deposit_check_3847(account_id, check_amount), where check_amount is the amount of the check in USD; the customer must submit it themselves in the app (agent cannot deposit on their behalf). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_011]
Setting balance and deposit alerts is the documented way to track funds availability of deposits. [doc_business_checking_accounts_sky_blue_007]

facts_found: transfer_to_human_agents reason codes are organized into 4 priority tiers and the agent must always select from the highest tier that applies. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]
Tier 1 code 'technical_system_error' is defined as: System error or outage preventing completion of the customer's request. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Tier 1 code 'account_ownership_dispute' is scoped to ownership disputes, joint account issues, or identity verification failures requiring specialist — not to missing/unlinked account records for an already-verified customer. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Tier 2 codes apply when the transfer is due to the agent's inability to find or verify information (unconfirmed_external_communication, kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer, specialized_department_required, accessibility_or_special_needs). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]
Tier 3 'customer_requests_human_no_specific_reason' applies only when the customer requests a human without a clear reason and is not frustrated. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]
Tier 4 'other' is a catch-all used only when none of the above reasons apply, and requires a detailed explanation in the summary field. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

The KB has no documented procedure for a verified customer whose profile returns zero bank accounts; the nearest documented handling is the CODE 52 'No Checking Account' status check, which for an account that exists and is OPEN but still errors attributes it to a system synchronization issue (wait 10-15 minutes and retry). [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

General troubleshooting escalation guidance: escalate when the issue persists across devices/networks after the user runs refresh_cache() and signs back in, when specific error codes or repeated failures occur, or for security concerns/account access lockouts. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_002]

For persisting errors the documented steps are to capture screenshots, timestamps and the exact workflow, verify device/browser/app version, and escalate with logs if multiple attempts produce the same result. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

Mandatory pre-transfer internal-tool sequences exist only for specific scenarios: the 11/13 backend payment-reflection incident (initial_transfer_to_human_agent_1822 then initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218, regular transfer only on the third request) and the credit-card purchase-decline protocol (initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 for the first three requests, regular transfer on the fourth). [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_011]
The credit-card decline protocol requires using the regular transfer_to_human_agents tool only on the fourth transfer request for that scenario. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_010]

No KB document names the exact parameter signature of transfer_to_human_agents; it only states that a reason code is selected when using the tool and that a 'summary field' carries the detailed explanation. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

No KB document describes a specific handling procedure for a verified customer whose profile returns zero linked bank accounts (missing/unlinked internal records).

An authorization hold is a temporary hold on funds that are not available for use; holds may not appear in recent transactions immediately, but even without a visible line item they reduce the available balance until released or finalized. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_004]

Rho-Bank keeps a temporary hold on certain deposits (e.g., paycheck deposits that are then refunded), which can affect the available balance shortly after a deposit posts. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_004]

Pending card transactions and checks can decrease available funds before they appear as posted, which can cause a lower/negative available balance. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]
To review holds the customer is directed to check both pending and posted activity to understand current holds and recent payments. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

CODE 51 (insufficient funds) requires first looking up the checking account balance, and if the balance APPEARS sufficient, checking authorization holds and pending transactions — merchant holds typically release in 1-3 business days. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

Pending debits reduce available balance, and the account's overdraft_pos_enabled field (from the account lookup) shows whether POS overdraft coverage is opted in (Regulation E opt-in required). [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

Common decline reasons include the requested amount exceeding the AVAILABLE balance at the time of authorization and pending card holds temporarily reducing the available balance; confirmation is via the customer's decline notification and recent activity. The available balance is the ceiling for authorizations; a small buffer of up to 5 may be considered for minor adjustments, but spending beyond that results in declines. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_005]

Card purchases and ATM withdrawals are authorized only up to the available balance; a charge above available funds is declined immediately with no overdraft. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_003]
